scope: Experimental candidate and prospective adapter only; installed/running production excluded
disposition: AUDIT CONDITIONAL PASS — SPECIFIC REMEDIATIONS REQUIRED

findings.title: Qualified context and host-resource envelope is not enforced by the serving admission path
findings.status: CONFIRMED release-readiness gap; not a demonstrated allocation overflow
findings.mechanism: Service capacity is 65536; request admission compares widened logical-position + input + maximum generation against that allocation, not the qualified GPU-only limit 32768. The smaller environment capacity override is qualification-only. Host-memory reserve, RSS and GPU-load checks belong to test controllers, not ordinary HTTP admission.
findings.reproduction: Run python3 docs/audits/test_runtime_capacity.py. Actual extracted candidate function accepts position 32768 + input 1 + generation 1 at capacity 65536; rejects capacity+one and negative/overflow-sized accounting. No model allocation occurs.
findings.impact: A direct API client can enter unqualified CPU-fallback territory and consume resources beyond the approved operational envelope. Existing allocation-bound enforcement prevents the tested arithmetic overflow; no actual OOM or corruption is claimed.
findings.action: Before authorizing a GPU-only release, enforce total logical context plus requested generation <=32768 in a reviewed server configuration/path (including resident continuation); specify enforceable one-model and host-memory admission/abort policy. Retest before-mutation rejection. Operational instructions alone must not be described as runtime enforcement.
findings.mandatory: Required for the proposed bounded 32K serving envelope.

findings.title: Deployment ownership and complete rollback provenance remain unverified
findings.status: CONFIRMED prerequisite gap; production intentionally not inspected
findings.mechanism: Neither a historical Git checkout nor old binary/shader hashes identifies the current installed executable build source, owning launcher, environment or exact restart command. The document correctly makes these contingent, so it is a review procedure rather than an executable approved deployment plan.
findings.reproduction: Static comparison of procedure preconditions and the two Git baselines; no production inventory is authorized or performed.
findings.impact: A future switch cannot yet prove that the correct process is stopped, all dependencies are installed together, or rollback reconstructs the old service/cache state.
findings.action: An independently authorized operator must identify launcher/owner and executable mapping, archive and hash binary + matching runtime shaders/dependencies + flags/environment + both cache directories, verify restoration, pin reviewed build/toolchain/model identities, and write exact owned-process start/stop/rollback commands. Resolve these at authorization, not by guessing during this audit.

findings.title: Work B fixed ten-minute total deadline conflicts with long-prefill support
findings.status: CONFIRMED source and bounded mock reproduction; live A+B not executed
evidence: Work A measured mask63 prefill 1174-1180s at16K and5084-5129s at32K
findings.mechanism: completionEvents defaults to totalMs=600000 and starts a non-resetting total timer before fetch. SSE comments refresh only idle timeout. The shipped generator exposes neither a timeout override nor a phase-aware deadline. Frequent keepalives therefore cannot preserve a legitimately long request.
findings.reproduction: Run node docs/audits/test_adapter_total_deadline.cjs WORK_B_EXPORT/clients/lmstudio-documents/dist/transport.js. It mocks fetch with comments every5ms: total100ms aborts despite idle40ms remaining healthy. Actual default is600000ms. No socket/service/model is used.
findings.impact: Combined long-prefill client support is not established. Adapter has a conservative serialized-byte input cap, so not every native16K/32K request is reachable through it; this does not establish that all allowed requests finish within600s. Native-only correctness is unaffected.
findings.action: Define the adapter supported latency/context envelope. For long-prefill support, make bounded deadlines configurable/phase-aware with explicit cancellation and test keepalive versus idle/total semantics; otherwise clearly exclude requests that may exceed600s. Do not silently remove all deadlines.
findings.mandatory: Required if this adapter is advertised for the proposed long-prefill envelope; may be excluded from a native-only release.

findings.title: Combined agent, actual Gateway and current GUI feature claims lack end-to-end qualification
findings.status: CONFIRMED evidence gap, not a demonstrated Gateway defect
findings.mechanism: Work B is not integrated in A. MCP tests exercise fixture servers, not real Gateway registry collision handling, dispatch binding or cursor aggregation. Work B reports installed service unreachable/current GUI NOT RUN. Historical Oct26 GUI observations predate this revision. Actual generated-model tools against the combined candidate are not established by mocked SSE/schema tests.
findings.reproduction: Inspect pinned reports, test fixture scope and PR discussion chronology; run npm build/test on an isolated B subtree. No actual Gateway implementation was found in the candidate/B changes, and no external Gateway is presumed.
findings.impact: Cannot advertise verified actual MCP registration/pagination or current LM Studio GUI/tool behavior from these tests. Native enable_thinking and effort none/low/medium/high are ignored; post-tool answer text in the same native completion is rejected/recovered. These limitations must be part of the supported contract.
findings.action: Either exclude these clients/features from the release envelope or qualify an isolated combined source selection with actual Gateway registration/pagination, GUI cancellation/follow-up and live tool calls. Test thinking translation and post-tool answer policy explicitly. Preserve stateless/full-history versus optional resident helper distinctions. No merge is authorized here.
findings.mandatory: Required only for feature claims included in the supported release; exclusions must be explicit.

findings.title: Intended-capacity performance acceptance remains undecided and partially evidenced
findings.status: CONFIRMED acceptance/evidence gap; numerical result not withdrawn
findings.mechanism: Most long trials are n=1 and cross-date. Scalar32K warm is interrupted; completed scalar cold cannot stand in for a process pair. Mask63 warm32K is5084.331s versus retained ordinary3145.699s, but ordinary is numerically unqualified and staging/cache confounds prevent causal attribution. No accepted production latency target or explicit waiver of the stated complete-three-way gate is supplied.
findings.reproduction: Recompute first128 phase records in retained logs: stage49.685588->747.928412s versus full-rowwise52.196747->54.655568s; inspect completed request/trial statuses separately.
findings.impact: Numerical readiness does not establish acceptable service latency. Current evidence cannot justify an uncontended regression percentage, run-to-run variance, or ordinary-N128 promotion.
findings.action: Architect must accept documented latency and the incomplete comparison within a restricted envelope, or require targeted matched follow-up under controlled conditions. Missing scalar warm need not be a universal hard blocker to a strictly limited, separately authorized canary; it remains an unclosed declared gate until explicitly dispositioned. This audit authorizes no canary.
findings.mandatory: Required performance disposition before final release authorization; a full rerun is not required for this audit.

findings.title: Evidence gates rely on Python assertions that optimization removes
findings.status: CONFIRMED bounded reproduction; recorded normal-mode PASS remains valid
findings.mechanism: Critical source/binary/fingerprint/tolerance checks use assert. Python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE removes them; a synthetic state error1.0 is accepted by the same gate under optimization and rejected normally.
findings.reproduction: python3 docs/audits/test_gate_optimization.py executes both modes on temporary synthetic evidence only.
findings.impact: Future optimized controller invocations can report validated evidence without performing gates. Existing recorded commands use normal Python; no material integrity defect in their actual results was found, and the independent checker uses explicit exceptions.
findings.action: Replace release-critical assertions with explicit validation exceptions or fail closed when __debug__ is false; add optimized-interpreter regression coverage.
findings.mandatory: Nonblocking hardening for the audited normal-mode evidence; do before relying on arbitrary controller invocation environments.

findings.title: Directory durability errors are ignored after checkpoint rename
findings.status: CONFIRMED static control-flow finding; no power-loss experiment
findings.mechanism: File fsync, close and rename are checked, but directory open/fsync failures do not affect success and pruning proceeds. Atomic visibility is supported; fully acknowledged directory-entry durability is not guaranteed by this return path.
findings.reproduction: Static proof: if open(directory) fails or fsync(dir_fd) returns-1, ok stays true and pruning executes. No disk fault or checkpoint mutation beyond the isolated synthetic test was induced.
findings.impact: After a crash/power loss, a reported saved checkpoint may be missing; loader should reject/rebuild. This is a cache durability/observability limitation, not demonstrated acceptance of corrupt state.
findings.action: Check/report directory-open/fsync outcomes distinctly, avoid claiming guaranteed crash durability and avoid pruning the last recoverable predecessor before durability policy succeeds. Do not pretend a post-rename failure restores the old file.
findings.mandatory: Nonblocking cache durability improvement within rebuild-on-miss design.
